name: Veltran MedSync Post-Op Compression Suit
description: Full-body compression garment in clinical off-white with color-coded gradient banding — blue at the extremities grading to warm amber at the core — indicating zone-specific compression levels. Issued post-augmentation surgery or major geneware integration. Micro-conductive threads embedded in the fabric monitor swelling, temperature differentials, and tissue resistance, transmitting passive data to a paired BCI or clinic receiver. Seams are laser-bonded rather than stitched to prevent irritation at surgical margins. Zipper channels allow access without full removal.
functionality: Biometric monitoring of post-surgical sites via BCI or external receiver; graduated compression by body zone; zipper-access panels for wound care without removal; anti-microbial fabric for extended wear during recovery.
what_it_says: You've been rebuilt recently — and whether the procedure was elective or emergency says everything about who paid for it.
worn_by: anyone who just spent serious Φ on body modification
manufacturer: Veltran Medical Fabrics — Helix Corp subsidiary
price_range: Φ120–Φ340 (sometimes covered by employer medical plans at Tier 3+)
story_hooks: A Tier 2 factory worker is wearing a Veltran suit weeks after their employer's mandatory chrome-arm replacement — the biometric data it's been logging would be very interesting to a labor attorney.
The clinic that issued this suit closed suddenly; the data receiver it paired to is now broadcasting to an unknown address.
Someone is wearing this under street clothes, months past any normal recovery window — either they never healed right, or they don't want anyone to know what was done to them.
related_entities: Ringo Corponation SlipThread MX-3 Urban Cable Micro-Mobility Rig

physical_description.visual_profile: A clinical, second-skin silhouette that clings to every anatomical contour. The garment reads as medical-grade despite its sleek form — sterile precision disguised as fashion. Gradient banding creates a subtle visual hierarchy from limbs to torso, invoking both hospital protocol and avant-garde minimalism. On-body it suggests either fresh augmentation or voluntary biometric optimization.
physical_description.fit: Compression-tight throughout, following musculature and bone structure without bunching. No excess fabric. Strategically graduated tension — maximum at wrists, ankles, and shoulders; looser at joints to allow micro-articulation. Allows full range of motion despite the snug embrace.
physical_description.primary_material: Medical-grade synth-elastane composite woven with micro-conductive filament threads (copper-aluminum blend). Base is off-white clinical textile, brushed matte finish to reduce glare during medical imaging.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost slick to the touch with a barely-perceptible ribbed micro-weave. Seams are flush and sealed — no traditional stitching texture. Where conductive threads surface near banding zones, subtle ridging creates a tactile map of monitoring zones.
physical_description.color_scheme: Off-white base (clinical, sterile tone). Gradient color banding: deep cerulean blue at wrists and ankles, transitioning through teal and sage at mid-limbs, warm amber-gold at chest and core. Banding is approximately 2cm wide at each zone transition.
physical_description.closures: Discrete laser-bonded seam channels with magnetic-snap zipper gates positioned at left forearm, right calf, and spine (back of neck to sacrum). Allows targeted access for medical inspection or augmentation site management without full removal.
distinctive_features: Embedded micro-conductive thread network visible as faint silvery tracery beneath surface material
Color-coded compression gradient zones corresponding to medical compression standards
Laser-sealed seams throughout to prevent post-op irritation
Magnetic zipper channels with subtle Veltran logo embossed near each gate
Subcutaneous sensor anchor points (slight raised dots) at major nerve clusters
Helix Corp subsidiary watermark printed at sternum in non-gloss ink
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2–3 crossover. Issued by medical institutions or corporations covering augmentation costs. Wearing one signals recent bio-modification, corporate health coverage, or voluntary optimization protocol. Not accessible to Tier 5 unless black-market salvage.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearer is either freshly augmented, recovering from geneware integration, or actively managing biometric compliance. Signals medical legitimacy, corporate investment in one's body, or voluntary self-optimization. Seen in clinic corridors, Helix facilities, and among chrome-positive communities. Fetishized by augmentation enthusiasts; stigmatized in unaugmented communities.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when newly issued; gradually shows micro-wear at magnetic closures and faint discoloration from skin oils along compression zones. Seams remain perfect indefinitely. After 2–3 months, the off-white yellows slightly at core if not regularly treated with medical textile whitener.
